Foundations.name: Tokens
Foundations.desc: The named values every component is built from. Use the semantic names, never raw colours.

Foundations.name: Motion
Foundations.desc: Motion is calm and explains where things came from. It is always optional and turns off under reduced motion.

Foundations.name: Responsive
Foundations.desc: One product, many screens. Layout changes at breakpoints; tokens and components do not.

stories.title: A table on a phone
stories.note: Each row becomes a card. The first column is the title, and the other columns wrap underneath it.

stories.title: Television
stories.note: Read from 3 metres: body text 24px or larger, safe area 5% on every side, one focusable thing at a time.

Foundations.name: Patterns
Foundations.desc: Whole screens that combine components. Copy these before inventing something new.

stories.title: Infinite scrolling table
stories.note: Keep the header sticky and show the total. Load more before people reach the end.

stories.title: Approval queue
stories.note: Tap a request to open it full screen, with Approve and Decline pinned at the bottom.

Foundations.name: App marks
Foundations.desc: The Reach app icon. Always the squircle, never stretched, never recoloured outside the palette.

Foundations.name: Brand
Foundations.desc: The lockup pairs the mark with the wordmark set in the display face.

Foundations.name: Typography
Foundations.desc: SF Pro on iOS and Roboto Flex on Android, set by the system. Body text is 17.

Foundations.name: Icons
Foundations.desc: Lucide, drawn at a 2px stroke. Icons support labels. They don’t replace them.

stories.title: When the name disagrees with the glyph

Foundations.name: Layout presets
Foundations.desc: Mobile screens follow one shell: status bar, top bar, large title, content, and a floating tab bar.

stories.title: Sidebar and aside
stories.note: On a phone, the aside becomes the detail screen you push to.

Foundations.name: Hierarchical layout
Foundations.desc: List and detail. Wide screens show both. Narrow screens push the detail on top of the list.

Foundations.name: Modal page
Foundations.desc: A task that takes over the screen until it’s done or cancelled: onboarding, a new request, an import.

Foundations.name: Layout primitives
Foundations.desc: Stack, Inline, Split, AutoGrid and Container. They handle spacing, so components never set their own margins.

stories.title: The same AutoGrid in three containers

Foundations.name: Scroll area
Foundations.desc: For fixed-height regions only. Page-level scroll is always the browser’s.

stories.title: Always visible
stories.note: Show the bar when people need to know there is more, as in pickers.

stories.title: A fixed panel with a scrolling body

Foundations.name: Separator
Foundations.desc: A hairline between groups. Try spacing first.

stories.title: When space is the better answer

Forms.name: Field
Forms.desc: The wrapper for every form control: the label above, the control, then a hint or an error below it. Only one message shows at a time.

stories.title: Caution
stories.note: Caution is for values that are allowed but unusual. It never blocks saving.

Forms.name: Input
Forms.desc: The bare text control. Use it inside Field unless it labels itself, as a search box does.

Forms.name: NumberField
Forms.desc: For counts and amounts. Empty means no value, and it never turns into 0 by itself.

Forms.name: PasswordField
Forms.desc: Masked by default with a reveal button. Always allow pasting, so password managers work.

Forms.name: PinInput
Forms.desc: One box for each character. Typing moves to the next box, and pasting fills every box at once.

Forms.name: TagsInput
Forms.desc: A free list of short values, like skills or email addresses. Enter or a comma adds a tag. Backspace in an empty input removes the last one.

Forms.name: Rating
Forms.desc: Pick a whole number from 1 to 5. Always say what each number means, because a star alone is ambiguous.

Forms.name: Select
Forms.desc: Pick one value from a short, fixed list. Over about 10 options, use Combobox instead.

Forms.name: Combobox
Forms.desc: Type to filter a long list. Matches are highlighted, and Enter picks the first one.

Forms.name: Checkbox
Forms.desc: For turning options on or off as part of a form you then save. For a setting that applies straight away, use Switch.

Forms.name: RadioGroup
Forms.desc: Pick exactly one of two to five options when everyone needs to see the choices side by side.

Forms.name: Switch
Forms.desc: For a setting that applies the moment you flip it. If it takes a moment, show a spinner and roll back if it fails.

Forms.name: Toggle
Forms.desc: A button that stays pressed. Use it for view options and formatting, not for settings.

Forms.name: Slider
Forms.desc: For picking a rough value where the range matters more than the exact number. Pair it with a number input when the exact value matters.

Forms.name: Calendar
Forms.desc: A month grid for picking days. It shows leave, holidays and blocked days so you don’t have to guess.

Forms.name: DatePicker
Forms.desc: A field that opens a calendar. You can always type the date instead.

Forms.name: Typed fields
Forms.desc: Fields for a specific kind of value. Each one brings the right keyboard, format and checks.

Forms.name: ImageUploader
Forms.desc: Upload images with a preview. It checks size and file type before uploading, and says exactly what went wrong.

stories.title: AvatarUploader — the photo is the control

Forms.name: Dropzone
Forms.desc: A large target for dragging files onto. Clicking it always opens the file browser too.

Forms.name: RichTextEditor
Forms.desc: Formatted text for policies, notes and comments. It stores safe HTML and reads it back the same way.

stories.title: What it stores, and how it reads back

Forms.name: FileUploader
Forms.desc: Upload documents with a row for each file. Each row shows progress, lets you retry, and says why a file was refused.

Forms.name: TimePicker
Forms.desc: Pick a time with the system wheel. You can type the time with a hardware keyboard.

Forms.name: Form sections
Forms.desc: How long forms are laid out: titled sections, one column on phones, and a save bar that only appears once something has changed.

stories.title: Read, then edit
stories.note: Most profile data is read far more often than it’s edited, so show values first and edit in place.

Components.name: Accordion
Components.desc: Hide sections people only sometimes need. If most people need it, don’t hide it.

stories.title: With a status in the header

Components.name: AlertDialog
Components.desc: Interrupts to confirm something that can’t be undone. Name the action on the button, never just OK.

stories.title: When an undo is better
stories.note: If the action can be undone, skip the dialog. Do it straight away and offer Undo.

Components.name: Avatar
Components.desc: A person’s photo or initials. Initials get a stable colour worked out from the name.

Components.name: Badge
Components.desc: A short status or count. Tone carries meaning, so use it the same way everywhere.

stories.title: Sensitive
stories.note: Mark sensitive data with a lock so people know who else can see it.

Components.name: Breadcrumb
Components.desc: Shows where you are in a hierarchy. Every item except the last is a link.

Components.name: Button
Components.desc: One primary per view. Labels are verbs that say exactly what happens.

stories.title: Loading
stories.note: Keep the width steady and the label in place. The spinner takes the icon’s spot.

Components.name: Card
Components.desc: A surface that groups related content. Don’t nest cards inside cards.

Components.name: Chat
Components.desc: Direct messages about a request or a person. Your messages sit on the right in indigo.

Components.name: Clipboard
Components.desc: Copy a value in one tap. Confirm it in place, so there’s no toast to chase.

Components.name: ContextMenu
Components.desc: Long-press a row to open its actions. Every action must also be available somewhere you can see.

stories.title: On table rows, with the same commands elsewhere
stories.note: The row’s ⋯ button opens the same menu, so the actions are always discoverable.

Components.name: Dialog
Components.desc: A focused task over the page. Esc and the close button always dismiss it. On a phone it becomes a sheet.

Components.name: Dropdown menu
Components.desc: A list of actions or options behind a button.

Components.name: Feedback
Components.desc: Alerts, skeletons and empty states: how the page tells you what’s going on.

Components.name: Kbd
Components.desc: Shows a keyboard key. On touch devices, hide shortcuts or leave them out.

Components.name: Nav
Components.desc: Section navigation for the sidebar. On a phone, top-level sections move to the tab bar.

Components.name: Popover
Components.desc: Extra content or controls anchored to a trigger. It closes when you click outside it.

Components.name: Progress
Components.desc: Shows how far along something is. Use indeterminate only when you really can’t tell.

Components.name: Reveal
Components.desc: Animates content in and out without layout jumps. It respects reduced motion.

Components.name: Sheet
Components.desc: Slides up from the bottom for choices and short tasks. Drag it down or tap outside to close.

stories.title: A record opened from a queue

Components.name: Spinner
Components.desc: For short waits on a single thing. For whole areas, use skeletons.

Components.name: Stepper
Components.desc: Shows progress through a flow with a fixed number of steps. More than 5 steps is too many.

stories.title: Clickable completed steps
stories.note: Finished steps are links back. Future steps can’t be clicked until the current one is valid.

Components.name: Tabs
Components.desc: Switch between views of the same thing. Don’t use tabs to move through steps.

Components.name: Timeline
Components.desc: Events in order: history, approvals and changes that take effect on a set date.

Components.name: Toast
Components.desc: Brief confirmation after an action. It goes away by itself, so never put anything essential in one.

stories.title: When it should not be a toast
stories.note: If people must act on it or would miss it, use a dialog or an inline alert.

Components.name: Tooltip
Components.desc: Phones have no hover. Use visible labels instead, or long-press on icon-only controls.

stories.title: What not to put in one
stories.note: If it needs a sentence, use a popover or put the text on the page.

Components.name: Chip
Components.desc: Compact, tappable choices. Filter chips narrow results, input chips hold values, and suggestion chips offer a next step. For a status, use a Badge.

stories.title: Filter chips
stories.note: More than one can be on at a time. The tick shows the state, so it doesn’t rely on colour alone.

stories.title: Choice chips
stories.note: Exactly one is on, like a radio group.

Components.name: Segmented control
Components.desc: Switches between 2 to 5 views of the same content. Use it when the options are short and equally important.

Components.name: Floating button
Components.desc: The single most important action on a screen, floating above the content and the tab bar. One per screen, never destructive.

stories.title: Shrinks as you scroll
stories.note: The label collapses when scrolling down and returns when scrolling up.

stories.title: Speed dial
stories.note: Three actions at most. The scrim dims the page, and tapping it closes the menu.

Components.name: Banner
Components.desc: A full-width message at the top of the page about the whole app or account. Only one banner shows at a time.

Components.name: Notification centre
Components.desc: Everything that needs your attention, in one list. Unread items are tinted, and an item you can act on has its buttons inline.

Components.name: AI chat widget
Components.desc: An assistant that answers questions from your policies and data, and can take action once you confirm. It cites its sources, and it always says when it’s unsure.

stories.title: Launcher
stories.note: The nudge shows once per session and never covers a primary action.

stories.title: Streaming
stories.note: The send button becomes Stop. Text streams in, but the layout never jumps under the reader.

Components.name: Tertiary navigation
Components.desc: Moves between sections of one screen. On a phone it’s a scrolling row of pills under the title, or a list you drill into.

stories.title: Under primary tabs
stories.note: Line tabs for the area, and pills for the view inside it. Never put two rows of line tabs on top of each other.

stories.title: As a table of contents
stories.note: The current section is highlighted as you scroll. Clicking a section jumps to it smoothly, or instantly under reduced motion.

Components.name: Grouped navigation
Components.desc: A long list of destinations in labelled groups, like Settings. Each row pushes a new screen.

stories.title: Collapsible groups
stories.note: Open and closed groups are remembered for each person. The group holding the current page always opens.

stories.title: Nested
stories.note: On a phone each level is its own screen, so there’s never an indented tree.

Components.name: App bars
Components.desc: The bars above and below the content: a large title that collapses as you scroll, and a floating tab bar for the top-level sections.

stories.title: Glass on scroll
stories.note: Once content scrolls under it, the bar turns to glass and the large title shrinks into it.

Components.name: Command palette
Components.desc: Search everything and run actions from one field. On a phone it opens full screen from the search button.

Components.name: Action sheet
Components.desc: A short list of actions that slides up from the bottom. The destructive action is red, and Cancel always sits apart.

stories.title: With a title and a destructive action

Components.name: Hover card
Components.desc: A peek at a person or record. On a phone, long-press opens the preview and its actions.

Components.name: List item
Components.desc: The row that most lists are built from. The content in the middle is always the same, and what goes before and after it changes.

Components.name: Carousel
Components.desc: Shows a few equal items side by side, where people swipe or scroll to see more. The next card always peeks in from the edge.

stories.title: With controls
stories.note: Arrow buttons for pointer users, swipe for touch, and the arrow keys when it has focus. It never auto-plays.

Components.name: Coach mark
Components.desc: Introduces one new feature, pointing at the actual control. Use it sparingly, and never for things a good label could explain.

Data.name: Table
Data.desc: On a phone, each row becomes a card. The first column is the title, the key values sit underneath it, and tapping the card opens the detail.

stories.title: Numeric alignment
stories.note: Right-align numbers and money, and use the same number of decimals down the whole column.

stories.title: Interactive rows
stories.note: The whole card is tappable, and the chevron shows it opens something.

stories.title: DataTable: sorting
stories.note: Click to sort, click again to reverse. Shift-click adds a second sort, and the small numbers show the order.

stories.title: DataTable, all of it at once

Data.name: ColumnChooser
Data.desc: Lets people pick and reorder table columns. Their choice is saved for each table.

Data.name: FilterBuilder
Data.desc: Build filters out of conditions. Applied filters then show as chips above the results.

Data.name: Kanban
Data.desc: Move work between stages. Drag with a mouse or a finger, or use the keyboard or the card menu. Every drag has a non-drag alternative.

stories.title: Limits and locked columns
stories.note: A full column refuses drops and says why. A locked column still shows its cards, but you can’t move them.

stories.title: The gap opens in both columns
stories.note: The card’s old spot stays open until you drop it, so there’s always a clear way back.

stories.title: Adding and deleting sections
stories.note: Deleting a section that has cards asks where to move them first.

stories.title: Every column long
stories.note: Each column scrolls on its own, and the headers stay in place.

Data.name: KeyValues
Data.desc: Label and value pairs for record details. Keys are quiet and values are clear.

Data.name: Money
Data.desc: Money stays exact. It’s stored in minor units, formatted for the locale, and always shown with its currency.

Data.name: Pagination
Data.desc: On a phone, pagination is "Page 3 of 52" between two arrows. Lists usually load more as you scroll instead.

Data.name: SortableList
Data.desc: Reorder a short list by dragging. Keyboard and screen readers are supported, and every move is announced.

stories.title: Rows that say what they are

Data.name: Stat
Data.desc: One number with context. Direction and sentiment are separate: fewer leavers is down, and that’s good.

Data.name: VirtualList
Data.desc: Renders only the rows you can see, so 20,000 rows scroll smoothly. Row heights can vary.

Data.name: Complex filters
Data.desc: For big lists: saved views, facets with counts, nested and/or groups, and a way back when nothing matches. Every filter is shown as a chip you can remove.

stories.title: Facets with counts
stories.note: Counts update as you pick, and an option with 0 results is dimmed but can still be picked.

stories.title: Nested and/or groups
stories.note: Two levels of groups at most. The plain-language summary underneath is what people actually read.

stories.title: Query syntax
stories.note: For power users. Every token turns into the same chip you’d get from the menus.

stories.title: Zero results, with a way out

Data.name: Tree view
Data.desc: Nested items such as folders, departments or cost centres. Arrow keys move through it, and branches load when you open them.

stories.title: With checkboxes
stories.note: Checking a parent checks all its children. If only some children are checked, the parent shows a dash.

stories.title: Drag to move
stories.note: Dropping onto a folder moves the item into it, and the folder is outlined while you hover.

Data.name: Scheduler
Data.desc: A day view with a strip of dates, plus an agenda list. On a phone, the week view only works in landscape.

stories.title: Clashes
stories.note: Overlapping events sit side by side, and a real clash has a red outline.

Charts.name: Overview
Charts.desc: Every chart puts the number first and the chart under it. One colour means one series, and categories use the chart palette in order.

stories.title: Zoom, drag and right-click
stories.note: Pinch to zoom and drag to pan. Long-press opens the menu.

Charts.name: Bar
Charts.desc: Compare amounts. Vertical bars suit periods of time, and horizontal bars suit named categories.

Charts.name: Trend
Charts.desc: How a value changes over time. The line is the data and the dashed line is the plan. Nothing else.

stories.title: Small multiples
stories.note: Same scale, same size, one per team. Easier to compare than four lines on one chart.

stories.title: Hover, click and legend toggles
stories.note: Click a legend item to hide that series. The hidden one is struck through, and the axis rescales.

Charts.name: Distribution
Charts.desc: Parts of a whole. Use it for up to six parts, and go biggest first.

Charts.name: Heatmap
Charts.desc: Intensity across two dimensions, such as when people take leave. Darker means more.

stories.title: A fixed scale
stories.note: When you compare heatmaps, lock them to one scale. Otherwise the same colour means different numbers.

Charts.name: Funnel
Charts.desc: How many make it through each stage. Look at the drop between stages, not the stages themselves.

Charts.name: Timeline (Gantt)
Charts.desc: Who is doing what, and when. Lanes are people or projects, and bars are periods of time.

stories.title: Zoom, drag and select
stories.note: Drag across empty days to select a range, then create leave or cover for those days.

stories.title: When items collide
stories.note: Overlapping items stack into rows. A real conflict gets a red outline.

Charts.name: Org chart
Charts.desc: On a phone the org chart is a tree you expand and collapse. Tap a person to open their profile, and use "View as chart" for the full canvas.

stories.title: Pan and zoom
stories.note: Pinch the canvas view to zoom.

stories.title: Search, focus and the chain
stories.note: Search dims everyone else and highlights the chain of managers up to the top.

stories.title: Nothing moves under the pointer
stories.note: Opening or closing a branch keeps the card you clicked exactly where it is. The rest of the chart shifts around it.

stories.title: Drag to change a reporting line
stories.note: Drop Mei on Tom to make him her manager. We ask you to confirm first, and the change takes effect from a date you choose.

stories.title: Selecting a person
stories.note: Click or press Enter to select. The arrow keys move up, down and along the tree.

stories.title: Departments, collapsed
stories.note: Start collapsed to departments on big orgs. The number is the size of each branch, and clicking it expands one level.

stories.title: Span of control and vacancies
stories.note: A red outline flags a span over 7 direct reports. Open roles are shown as dashed cards.

Charts.name: Movement
Charts.desc: How a number got from start to end. Green adds, red takes away, and indigo is a total.

stories.title: When it goes negative
stories.note: Below zero, the axis line becomes the reference, so the bars hang under it.

Charts.name: Pay
Charts.desc: Salary bands and fairness. These charts are sensitive, so they only show to people who can see pay.

Charts.name: Combo
Charts.desc: Bars and a line on one chart, when two measures share a time axis but have different units. Label both axes.

Charts.name: Stacked area
Charts.desc: How a total changes over time, and what makes it up. Keep it to five layers or fewer, with the biggest at the bottom.

Charts.name: Gauge
Charts.desc: Progress toward one target. Show the number large, and use a gauge only where "how close are we" is the question.

Charts.name: Radar
Charts.desc: Compares a few items across five to eight qualities, such as skills in a review. For precise comparisons, use bars.

Charts.name: Treemap
Charts.desc: Parts of a whole when there are too many parts for a donut. The size of each area is its value.

Charts.name: Histogram
Charts.desc: How values are spread, such as salaries or tenure. The bars touch because the ranges are continuous.

Charts.name: Cohort
Charts.desc: How each group of joiners stays over time. Read across a row for one cohort, and down a column to compare cohorts.

Charts.name: Bullet
Charts.desc: One measure against a target and qualitative ranges. It fits many targets into far less space than gauges.

Charts.name: Calendar heatmap
Charts.desc: Activity per day across months, such as sick days or check-ins. Darker means more.

Charts.name: Bubble
Charts.desc: A scatter plot where bubble size is a third value. Label the bubbles directly, and keep it to around a dozen.

Charts.name: KPI dashboard
Charts.desc: How charts combine on one screen: numbers first, one hero chart, and supporting charts in a grid.
